wiki-iran.standing: The Persian-language and English encyclopedia entry for a country of some 90 million people, straddling the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. Readership rises when Iran is at the centre of a sanctions fight, a nuclear question or a shipping crisis.
wiki-iran.recent: The peak on 25 August fell in the week Treasury named nearly 60 entities under "Operation Economic Outcast," the campaign Bessent built to reach every Iranian dollar, and Iran vowed to resist it. The same days carried the Hormuz dispute: Trump declared the strait clear while Iran and Oman charted only a temporary corridor.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is sold against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Brent sits well below its 23 July peak despite the IRGC declaring Hormuz closed to vessels transiting without Iranian coordination, a waterway carrying a fifth of the world's oil. Traffic collapsed to a single gas carrier on Monday, but China cut oil imports 45% and inventory absorbed the disruption before price did.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of American light sweet crude, the benchmark US oil is priced against and the reference for fuel costs across North America. It moves on supply, storage and policy, and refiners, airlines and drivers pay for the change.
wti.recent: Crude has given back its summer war premium. Prices ran above $91 in mid-August after Trump signaled he won't renew the Iran deal and Iran's Azizi issued warnings over Hormuz, but the disruption never reached barrels: China cut oil imports 45%, Pakistan opened bonded fuel tanks, and inventory absorbed the chokepoint before price did.

natgas-hh.standing: The U.S. benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub and used to price most American gas contracts. It sets what households pay to heat and cook, what power plants pay to run, and what fertiliser and chemical makers pay for feedstock.
natgas-hh.recent: Gas has drifted down about 12% over two months, from $3.34 on Jun 30 to $2.70, with the floor at $2.56 on Aug 7. Supply news has run the same direction: Pakistan Petroleum struck gas in Chiltan rock at Sujawal, and Iran reported 161 billion cubic meters recoverable in Fars province.

wheat.standing: The world price of a tonne of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. It moves on weather, harvests and export policy in a handful of big producers, and bread, flour and feed prices follow it.
wheat.recent: Wheat has climbed roughly a third from its September 2025 low to $228.7 a tonne, and importers are absorbing it: Sindh will bring in 5 million tons after Pakistan withdrew its support price, while low water on the Rhine has cut barge draughts on one of Europe's main grain routes. Buyers in Africa are shifting toward cassava and sorghum flour.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple grain for roughly half the planet and the one whose cost is felt fastest in Asian and West African household budgets. It moves on monsoon rains, harvests and export bans, and food-price inflation follows it.
rice.recent: The price has fallen 17.7% over the series, to $464 per tonne from a high of $563.8 in Aug 2024 and off a low of $330.6 in Oct 2025. The input does not name a cause for the move.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity. Demand tracks grids, buildings, motors and cabling, which is why its price is read as a gauge of how much the world is building and electrifying.
copper.recent: Copper sits near its series high of $13,550/mt, set in June 2026, roughly half again above the December 2024 low of $8,910. The pull is electrical: transformer designs are being reworked for AI power demand, EV charging is straining grid voltage, and Washington has banned foreign grid parts. In Zambia, a major producer, Hichilema won a second term.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the world's reference risk-free rate. It sets the floor under mortgages, corporate borrowing and the price of every other asset, and it rises when lenders demand more compensation for inflation or for holding Washington's paper.
us-10y.recent: The move belongs to the same repricing that took thirty-year yields to 5.3%, a 2007 level, as tariffs and war costs feed into expected inflation and the Treasury has intervened twice — buying yen alongside Japan and doubling its long-bond buyback. Traders are also positioning around Warsh's Jackson Hole speech and the Fed's independence.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies, and the default measure of American equity performance. Trillions in pension and index funds track it, so a company's admission to it forces buying by funds that must hold whatever it holds.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its Aug 13 high after a run driven by AI capital spending and unsettled by rates. Nvidia pledged $500 billion to finance its own buyers, while Fed minutes showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed and Treasury yields rose on strong services data. Reddit jumped 11% on an index committee's decision alone.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by a handful of very large technology firms, so it swings on what happens to chipmakers, cloud providers and consumer hardware more than on the wider economy.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits below its Jun 2 high of 30660 after a Jul 29 low of 27190. Nvidia guided to $108bn in revenue next quarter, and disclosed that it backstops $230 billion in customer lease obligations and pledged $500 billion to its own buyers. Meta settled child-safety claims for $17.1bn, roughly 1% of its stock value.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, averaged across grades and states. It follows crude, but refining capacity and taxes set the gap, and it is the most visible price in US politics.
us-gas-retail.recent: The pressure in this market is on refining, not crude. Ukrainian drone strikes hit Russian refineries, and Moscow rationed gasoline at 30 litres a station while Putin conceded fuel issues were unresolved and Novak said Russia would import fuel and lower standards. India cut its petrol export tax to nil, easing supply elsewhere.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of natural gas at the Dutch TTF hub, the benchmark for gas traded in northwest Europe. It sets what factories, power stations and households pay for heat and electricity, and it moves on pipeline supply, storage levels and weather.
natgas-ttf.recent: The series is monthly and runs to 1 July 2026, so it predates the month's gas news: it rose 47% from a December 2025 low of $9.46 to $17.93 in July, its highest in the window. The coverage since — a second Nord Stream sabotage suspect arrested in Croatia, and Iran's Fars province find of 161 billion cubic meters — postdates the reading.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders expect in the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from option prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear in equity markets.
vix.recent: Volatility drained out of markets through the window, with the index settling near its 14 August low of 14.25 after peaking at 22.22 on 10 June. The calm extended beyond equities: bitcoin's own volatility collapsed far enough that traders complained nothing really prints money in crypto, even as rising yields and Brent crude dragged equities lower.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's price against the dollar, and the pass-through for a country that imports most of its fuel, wheat and medicine. Every rupee of weakness raises the cost of what Pakistan buys abroad and of the dollar debt it owes.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat, holding within a rupee and a half of 277 all month, with the weakest print at 278.1 on Aug 7 and the strongest at 276.6 on Jul 31. Nothing in the month's news moved it: neither Sindh's plan to import 5 million tons of wheat nor K-Electric's withdrawal from the Fesco bid registered in the rate.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted against the dollar. It is priced off oil earnings and the central bank's willingness to let the rate float, and it sets the cost of nearly everything the country imports, from petrol to wheat.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed to 1342 from an Aug 8 high of 1365 as FTSE Russell moved to reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified to Frontier status on September 21, a change that routes index-tracking money back into Nigerian assets. Atiku Abubakar's pledge to restore the petrol subsidy in 2027 cuts the other way.

fx-egp.standing: The exchange rate of Egypt's currency against the US dollar. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel, so the pound's level sets the price of bread and energy for more than 100 million people and the cost of servicing state debt.
fx-egp.recent: The pound weakened after Washington cut off a major Egyptian bank from the global financial system on 28 August, part of a push by Bessent that also targeted banks in the UAE over Iran ties. The currency had reached 51.16 on 1 August and 49.56 on 8 August before settling near 50.26.

fx-try.standing: Turkey's currency, quoted as lira per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. It sets the price of everything Turkey imports — energy, machinery, grain — and it is the channel through which the country's interest-rate policy reaches household prices.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh low against the dollar, weakening about 1.5 percent over the month with no single break. The period's news was diplomatic rather than monetary: Turkey signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, sought an Interpol notice for Netanyahu over the Gaza flotilla case, and drew Moscow's complaint that a US arms transfer through Turkey to Ukraine 'undermines trust'.

fx-bdt.standing: The taka's price against the US dollar. Bangladesh imports its fuel, food staples and industrial inputs in dollars while earning them back through garment exports and remittances, so the rate sets the cost of living for a country of 170 million.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka has been close to flat over the month, easing from 124 on Aug 7 to 122 on Aug 19 before settling near 123.3. Politics moved faster than the currency: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected president on 21 August, and a tribunal in Dhaka has since put journalists on trial under rules that allow no constitutional challenge.

fx-idr.standing: Indonesia's currency, quoted as rupiah per US dollar, so a higher number means a weaker rupiah. It is the price at which Southeast Asia's largest economy trades its commodity exports and services its foreign-currency debt.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah firmed through August, from 18,070 on 31 July to 17,650 on 21 August. The coverage points to policy rather than markets: Prabowo's tightening state grip on the economy, a ruling that keeps millions of gig drivers as "partners" rather than employees, and RCEP's persistent gap between integrated goods trade and capital.

fx-lbp.standing: The exchange rate of Lebanon's currency against the US dollar. After the banking collapse it lost most of its value and was re-fixed at a far weaker level, so households, salaries and imported food, fuel and medicine are all priced through it.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has held near flat over the month, moving within a narrow band between 89,180 on Jul 31 and 89,720 on Aug 7 — a peg holding while the country around it does not. Lebanon's health ministry put the death toll from Israeli attacks at 4,350, and Israeli strikes killed 11 in Lebanon in mid-August.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the dollar, set within a daily band by the People's Bank of China rather than left fully to the market. It prices the world's largest exporter's goods, so it moves trade balances, tariffs and factory orders across Asia.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted stronger through August, from 6.755 on 4 August to 6.721 on 28 August, its firmest of the month. Beijing spent the period pushing back on Washington: Wang Yi told the US to "remove disruptions" before a summit, and China signalled it can resist Trump's economic threats over Iran. Chinese EV makers meanwhile absorbed EU car tariffs rather than passing them on.

fx-inr.standing: India's currency, quoted as rupees per US dollar, and the price at which the world's most populous economy pays for imported oil, fertiliser and machinery. A weaker rupee raises the cost of everything India buys abroad and the value of what its workers send home.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee has drifted about a tenth of a percent weaker over the month, ranging between 95.05 on Aug 5 and 95.77 on Aug 20 — a narrow band. Nothing in the period's India news explains the move: the milk price in Mumbai crossing Rs 100, the Javelin missile purchase in New Delhi, and the flood relief flown to Nepal all sit outside the currency's drivers.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate of Brazil's currency against the US dollar. Brazil is a major exporter of soy, iron ore, beef and oil, and the real tracks commodity demand, the country's interest-rate gap with the US, and its fiscal politics.
fx-brl.recent: The real weakened about 2 percent over the month, from 5.077 on Aug 3 to a low of 5.222 on Aug 15, and sits near 5.194. The month's Brazil news ran to the frontier rather than the currency: Petrobras reported signs of oil off the Amazon coast on Aug 17, which Lula called a "passport," and rising land conflicts inland.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate of Mexico's peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends the large majority of its exports to the United States, so the peso reacts fast to US trade policy and rate decisions.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened from 17.35 on Aug 1 to 16.92 by Aug 21 before easing to 17.03, a move of under two percent across the month. The input carries no Mexico-specific policy, trade or rate news that would explain the drift.

fx-eur.standing: The exchange rate between the euro and the US dollar, the world's most heavily traded currency pair. It reflects the gap between the European Central Bank and the Federal Reserve on rates and growth, and it sets the price of everything Europe imports in dollars — oil above all.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted lower across the month, from 0.8688 on Aug 4 to 0.8556 on Aug 20 before recovering to 0.8632. Brussels spent the period on Russia policy rather than growth: an autumn sanctions package described as the bloc's broadest, four member states pressing to unlock Russia's frozen assets, and war-driven fuel prices outrunning the EU's tariffs on Chinese cars.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate of Japan's currency against the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker yen. It is one of the world's most traded pairs and the funding leg of carry trades that reach far beyond Japan.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen held near 160 to the dollar across the month, drifting slightly stronger from its 160.6 high on Jul 31 to a 156.5 low on Aug 3 before returning to 160.1. Nothing in the month's Japan news — Putin's Kuril visit and the ambassador's summons, Takaichi skipping Yasukuni, the India trade delegation — moved the rate.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker ruble. It is the cleanest live price on Russia's war economy — sanctions, oil receipts and capital flight all land here first.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble lost about 8% against the dollar over the month as the Kremlin declared the peace talks dead and signalled escalation, Russia struck nine Ukrainian cities and Moscow moved to seize undefended factories. Households pulled 4.2 trillion rubles into cash over the same stretch.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, and one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. It swings on commodity prices, global risk appetite and domestic politics, and it sets the local cost of fuel and imported goods.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed through August, from 16.56 on Aug 1 to a low of 15.92 on Aug 26, a move the month's South African news does not account for: the domestic stories were fiscal and social rather than monetary — R88.6bn in unclaimed dormant accounts and pensions under Treasury review, and NSFAS improperly funding 40,000 students R5.1 billion.

btc.standing: The largest cryptocurrency by market value, traded around the clock on exchanges worldwide with no issuer and a fixed supply schedule. It trades as a bet on monetary policy and liquidity, and its swings set the tone for the rest of the crypto market.
btc.recent: The run from $62,770 on Aug 2 to $80,270 on Aug 28 was driven by positioning rather than buying: the surge to $80,020 came as short sellers were squeezed out, with $48 billion in futures open interest sitting against $25 billion in daily volume. Traders then held into Warsh's Jackson Hole speech.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by value, and the settlement layer for most tokens, stablecoins and decentralised finance. Its price reflects demand for that block space, and moves with regulation, exchange access and the flow of institutional money.
eth.recent: Ether rose about 27% over the month, from $1,843 on Aug 2 to a peak of $2,515 on Aug 22, alongside a run of regulatory openings: the US securities regulator proposed a crypto rulebook in a surprise announcement, weeks after the SEC scrapped its Reg Crypto vote. Wall Street put $11.2 billion into licensed venues.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by a physical ounce of gold in a vault, tracking the metal's spot price on crypto exchanges. It moves with the classic gold trade — currency debasement, central-bank credibility, war — but trades around the clock.
paxg.recent: Gold ran to $4,672 on Aug 25 as traders positioned around Warsh's Jackson Hole speech and what it signals about Fed independence, with bitcoin moving alongside it. Physical demand is visible too: street dealers in Kassala now outbid Sudan's licensed market, and thieves cut a bronze age gold collection out of a Spanish museum on Aug 27.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A daily count of how many people open the Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence. It rises and falls with public attention to the technology rather than with anything the technology does, making it a rough gauge of how far AI has spilled out of the trade press.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The 14 August peak came as attention turned to the money and machinery underneath the field rather than the models: Nvidia backstops $230 billion in customer lease obligations, Bullish is lending $100 million against GPUs that depreciate faster than the loans, and Alibaba is raising $10 billion in new equity for AI capex. Readership has since fallen back.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia — the country's population, history and government. It rises when Russia is at the centre of a story, and the shape of the curve tracks how long that story holds people's attention.
wiki-russia.recent: The 17 August peak followed Ukraine's largest attack of the war on 16 August and the EU foreign affairs chief's push to expand sanctions against Russia. Russian missiles killed at least 13 in Kyiv on 20 August, and by 27 August Kremlin sources had declared the peace talks dead.

wiki-pakistan.standing: The number of people reading the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan each day. It is a rough gauge of how much of the world's attention the country holds, and it rises when something there breaks into the news elsewhere.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The peak on 14 Aug fell on Pakistan's independence day, which the series climbs for every year. The larger story since came on 26 August, when a fire in the nursery of PIMS in Islamabad killed fourteen newborns; the government announced 5 million rupees per family before naming a cause. Attention has since fallen back.

wiki-china.standing: The Wikipedia article on China, and a daily count of how many people open it. Readership rises when the country is at the centre of a story — a border disaster, a trade fight, a diplomatic confrontation — so the curve marks the days China entered the news.
wiki-china.recent: The peak came as flash flooding tore through the Nepal-China border region, killing at least 160 and leaving hundreds missing at Rasuwagadhi, where a wall of water arrived with no rain before it. Beijing was in the news on two other fronts: Wang Yi telling Washington to "remove disruptions" before a summit, and China resisting Trump's sanctions push to isolate Iran.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that every tanker leaving the Gulf must pass through, roughly two miles wide at its shipping channels. It is the narrowest point in the world's oil trade, and no pipeline can replace what moves through it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: The 18 August peak followed a vessel being struck by an unknown projectile in the strait, days after traffic fell to single digits when the 60-day deadline for a US-Iran MoU expired. Readership stayed elevated through Rezaei's "not even one drop" warning, the Iran-Oman temporary corridor, and the IRGC's claim that Hormuz is closed to vessels transiting without Iranian coordination.

wiki-india.standing: The daily readership of Wikipedia's article on India, a rough gauge of global curiosity about the world's most populous country — a nuclear-armed democracy, a top-five economy, and a party to unresolved disputes over Kashmir, its Himalayan border and the rivers it shares.
wiki-india.recent: Attention peaked on 15 August, India's 80th Independence Day, as Modi renewed his 'aatmanirbhar Bharat' push on semiconductor plants and energy security. Interest has drained off since, though the Nepal flash floods have kept India in view: 288 Indians are missing, Delhi has airlifted 37.5 tonnes of aid and sent a tunnel rescue team for about 100 people trapped underground.

wiki-ukraine.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine each day. It is a rough gauge of public attention rather than of events, and it rises when a war that most readers follow intermittently forces itself back into view.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The peak on 24 August came as Ukraine's allies convened in Kyiv, where Zelenskyy said Patriot deliveries had halved since 2023 and Britain cleared MBDA to share SCALP missile component data with France and Ukraine. Attention then eased even as Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead and Zelensky called for 1,000 drones a day against Russia.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed to a handful of vessels a day: one gas carrier transited on Monday, and the IRGC Navy now says the strait is closed to any ship crossing without Iranian coordination. Rezaei tied resumption to an end to the wars in Gaza and Lebanon. Bahrain's output shrank 3.8%; China cut oil imports 45%.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits about a fifth below its June peak after a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu, and Saudi Arabia shelled villages in Razih district in Saada. Owners moving oil and containers between Asia and Europe are still routing around the strait rather than through it.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic sits near its 90-day baseline after a partial recovery from the June low, but the Red Sea has not settled: Houthi forces said they attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia on 24 August, and Pakistani nationals injured in an earlier Houthi attack in the Red Sea returned home this month.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has run about 8% below its own 90-day baseline, with the low of 170 vessels a day on Jul 19 well under the Jun 22 high of 264. The input names no closure or weather event at the strait itself — wave heights peaked at 0.6m — and the Houthi missile strike on a Saudi tanker off Yanbu sits on a different route.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic is running near its 90-day baseline, down 3.6% over the last week, with no weather alert and waves under 1.2 metres. The political temperature around the strait has risen without touching the shipping: Wang Yi told Washington to "remove disruptions" ahead of a summit, and Trump's planned chip tariffs — which the Computer & Communications Industry Association estimates at a $90 billion annual GDP hit — target the trade this lane carries.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits are running about 13% below their 90-day baseline, at 28 vessels a day against a peak of 83 on Jul 13. The canal authority moved on 21 August to cap daily transits in anticipation of a severe El Niño, the same drought pressure behind low water elsewhere. Separately, CK Hutchison is seeking HK$11.7b from Panama in a dispute over the canal ports.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has run about 6% below its 90-day baseline as attacks on Black Sea shipping mounted: three Greek vessels burned in three days to 18 August, and TASS says Russia has struck 130 ships since July. Grain and crude out of Odesa move through this water.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic sits near the bottom of its 85-day range, 119 vessels a day against a June 13 high of 163, with calm water — waves under 1.2m — ruling out weather. The input names no closure or rerouting in the strait itself; the sanctions campaign filling the same weeks targets banks and dollar access rather than Mediterranean transit.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic sits at 154 vessels a day, about 6 percent below its 90-day baseline, with rough seas and waves reaching 2.7 metres over the latest window. Nothing in the record ties the drop to a closure or dispute; the swing from 186 on Aug 1 to 126 two days later tracks weather, not politics.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic has swung hard with the risk further north: the run to 123 vessels on 31 July came days after tanker attacks pushed operators away from the Red Sea and Hormuz, where traffic fell to single digits around 17 August. A Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August. Seas were rough, with waves to 2.7m.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, roughly 97 percent below its own three-month baseline, with the last vessels recorded in mid-July. The collapse tracks a war with no diplomatic exit: Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead, Russia struck nine cities, and Zelensky called for 1,000 drones a day against Russia — a tempo that leaves no safe passage through a strait Ukraine can reach.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index reached 11,260 on 26 August, the top of a 36-day range that began at 10,700 on 15 July, as Riyadh's security and diplomatic position filled the news: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed a joint defence pact whose text is not public, and Trump submitted a Saudi nuclear deal to Congress that skips an enrichment ban.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits near the top of its 63-day range, having recovered from a 30 July low as Turkey's regional position hardened rather than broke. Ankara routed 70 long-range US missiles to Ukraine, drawing a Moscow complaint that the transfer undermines trust, and issued a genocide warrant for Netanyahu after Israeli strikes on the Idlib airbase near the Turkish border.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index has climbed 1.6% over the window despite the war: Iran fired two ballistic missiles at the UAE on 18 August, triggering Dubai's first emergency alert in months, and the UAE responded by suspending all trade and financial transactions with Iran. It has since eased from its 18 June high of 6,270.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index reached 1749 on Aug 26, then slipped as prosecutors charged former prime minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob with concealing assets. He pleaded not guilty in the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to failing to declare tens of millions of dollars — the third Malaysian ex-premier charged after leaving office, after Najib Razak and Muhyiddin Yassin.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index climbed through August as Prabowo's government tightened its grip on the economy, running more of it through cooperatives and state channels — a shift domestic investors have priced as directed spending rather than risk. It reached 6526 on Aug 21, up a fifth from its Jun 8 low of 5342.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index sits near the middle of its range, well below its Jun 25 high of 72,370 and above the Jul 29 low of 61,430, up 2.2% over the period. Nothing in the window explains the swing: the Japan news has been diplomatic and industrial — Russia's Kuril missile test after Tokyo's protest, and Piyush Goyal arriving with 200 Indian firms.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The Bank of Korea hiked rates to 3.00% on 27 August, the chip cycle setting the pace, and the index has given back 16% from its 22 June high of 9,115. Washington's cancellation of next month's Twin Dragons exercise landed alongside Lee's push to replace the armistice with a peace treaty.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a run of domestic news: Modi's renewed 'aatmanirbhar Bharat' push on semiconductor plants and energy security, an Indian purchase of Javelin missiles, and OpenAI making India the test market for ChatGPT ads with 50 brands. A data-centre build-out is drawing capital in. Mumbai milk crossing Rs 100 a litre points the other way.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed 13.93% over the past 64 days to a high of 5768 on Aug 17, with Singapore's role as a regional financial hub in evidence: crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion, and a 70-member Indian delegation arrived on Aug 19 for talks on tech, investment and trade ties.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after recovering from a Jul 30 low of 39930. Taipei indicted nine people, including an Nvidia manager, over AI server smuggling, while China's coast guard began patrolling east of Taiwan and Jakarta endorsed Beijing's claim to the island — pressure on the political frame around the chip trade, not on demand for it.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the top of its 37-day range, up about 5.5% from its 23 June low to a 17 July high it has returned to. Nothing in the Bangkok news of the period explains the climb: the run of Thai stories covers a jet ski rescue off a Thai island, the murder of Russian tourists in Pattaya, and a Deputy PM's offer of cybersecurity cooperation with Russia.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits at its 37-day high after a 7.4% run from its late-May low, and the political news out of Manila has not dented it: an ex-disbursing officer told the Senate impeachment court that Duterte ordered a P125-million confidential funds transfer. Nothing in that testimony touches the listed companies the index tracks.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a run from May, though it slipped on the last session. The move down came ahead of inflation data, the release traders had been positioned for. Corporate news was thin: KPMG Australia cut 27 partners and 360 staff, about 5% of its workforce.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index sits close to its high after Petrobras reported signs of oil off the Amazon coast on 17 August, a find Lula called a "passport" and one that bears directly on the state oil producer's weight in the index. The low on 18 August was recovered within days, leaving the series roughly flat over the window.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down about 5% over the past three months, from its Jun 2 high of 68,890 to a low of 63,930 on Aug 18, and sits near 65,480. Nothing in the available material explains the decline.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index has drifted down about 3% over the past three months, off its 22 July high of 3,380,000 and near the 19 August low of 2,874,000. The one Buenos Aires story in the window is an Interpol operation that dismantled a fraud network, with 58 arrested and 196 identified — nothing that explains the move in equities.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index held near its high through the breakdown of Canada-US trade talks: Washington imposed new tariffs on 22 August, Ottawa answered dollar for dollar with a list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, and Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened to cut power exports. Energy and mining weightings absorbed the shock.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index sits near its Aug 13 high of 7799 after climbing about 2% over the quarter, with a 0.72% gain on the day. Washington's "Operation Economic Outcast" sanctions campaign against Iran and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, where 7 tankers crossed Thursday, framed the period; a court also vacated the US ban on Anthropic. No single event in the record explains the move.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing over the period, with the high on Jul 29 and the low on Jun 9. Nothing in the London news of the past week explains the latest daily fall.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index sits near its 67-day peak of 26,440 on Aug 14, and the coverage in that window is mostly non-market: the EU's plan for its broadest Russia sanctions package, a second Nord Stream arrest in Croatia, and a malaria death among Frankfurt Airport workers. None of that explains the 4.4% climb from the Jun 10 low.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a 66-day climb, having peaked at 8,726 on Aug 10 and fallen 1.7% on the day to 8,320. The coverage window explains none of the swing: Paris news ran to the European Space Agency's €544 million award to three rocket startups and to EU crypto rules, neither of which moves the 40 largest listed French companies.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index sits near the top of its 66-day range, having climbed from its late-May low to a high on 13 August before easing back. Nothing in the Dutch news window explains the move: the period's stories were a low Rhine forcing draught restrictions and salt intrusion, and Fairphone taking its repairable handset to the US.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index has climbed nearly 9% over the window, reaching 20,210 on Aug 11 before easing to 19,880. Nothing in the available reporting explains the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up about five percent over the window, with the high on Aug 7 and a fall of just over one percent on the latest day. The input carries no Milan-specific event that explains the move.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range, up about 6% over that span, after climbing from 3,054 on Jun 10 to a high of 3,327 on Aug 5 and holding there since. Nothing in the window explains the move.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

xag.standing: A silver-backed token whose price tracks an ounce of physical silver held in vaults. Silver is both a monetary metal bought as a store of value and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics, brazing — so it moves on investment demand and factory demand at once.
xag.recent: The series more than doubled off its 6 August low of $29.81 before easing to $67.22 from a 28 August high of $69.42. The input does not identify what drove the move.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves as the case for a hike or a cut hardens — and every mortgage, deposit and dollar-funded borrower sits downstream of the answer.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The odds on no change fell to 39% on Aug 1 before recovering, peaking at 75% on Aug 15. They have since come back to 54%, squeezed after Fed minutes released on Aug 19 showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed; by Aug 27 traders were betting on hikes, with Bitcoin under $79,000 and XRP leading losses.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each escalation or de-escalation between Washington and Tehran rather than with any official assessment.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The bet has fallen by roughly two fifths since its 26% peak on Aug 2 as Washington pushed the confrontation onto financial ground rather than military: Treasury named nearly 60 entities under "Operation Economic Outcast" and cut six Banque Misr branches off from US dollar access. Trump declared Hormuz clear on Aug 25, and Iran and Oman charted a temporary corridor through the strait.

wiki-syria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Syria, a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking up the country's history, geography and politics rather than following a single story.
wiki-syria.recent: The 11 August peak sat between two clusters: on 18 August eight strikes hit an airbase in Idlib hours after four already had, Syria granted the IAEA access to an Assad-era undeclared nuclear site concealed for 18 years, and a court sentenced Wassim al-Assad to death. Washington then delisted Syria on 24 August, and the SDF dissolved into the army on 25 August.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the 45th and 47th US president, and one of the most-read biographies on the site. Its daily readership rises whenever Washington acts — a court ruling, a tariff, a strike order — making it a rough gauge of how far a decision travelled.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The 26 August peak followed a run of Iran decisions: widened US sanctions Tehran vowed to resist, a Saudi nuclear deal that skips an enrichment ban, and a declaration that Hormuz was clear. Courts pushed back at home, blocking mail-ballot curbs in Boston and voiding the Anthropic ban.

xmr.standing: A privacy-focused cryptocurrency that hides sender, receiver and amount by default, unlike Bitcoin's public ledger. That opacity makes it the settlement layer of choice for ransomware payments and sanctions evasion, and a standing problem for financial investigators.
xmr.recent: The rise tracks a run of enforcement and evasion news: CISA identified more than 200 Medusa ransomware victims over the past year, a Ukrainian developer went on trial in Bellinzona facing 12 years for his part in a ransomware operation, and North Korea's sanctions-evasion toolkit now earns revenue without touching banks.

wiki-stablecoin.standing: A cryptocurrency designed to hold a fixed value, usually one unit of a national currency, by holding reserves against every token issued. It is the settlement layer crypto uses for payments, and increasingly a rival to bank deposits.
wiki-stablecoin.recent: Banks moved onto the rails rather than around them: Shinhan built stablecoin rails with a card network, Standard Chartered began distributing Hong Kong's dollar stablecoin, and 39 state banking associations announced a rival chain. Crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion, while one paper put $700 billion of bank lending capacity at risk.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United States — a broad attention gauge that rises when the country itself, rather than any one American story, becomes the thing people want explained.
wiki-united-states.recent: The week's peak came as Washington pushed its Iran campaign outward: Treasury Secretary Bessent named the effort "Operation Economic Outcast" to bind third countries, Tehran denounced it, and China's Wang Yi told Washington to "remove disruptions" before a summit. Courts pushed back at home, blocking Postal Service mail-ballot rules and voiding an Anthropic blacklist.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The number of people reading Wikipedia's Bitcoin article each day — a rough gauge of public curiosity about the asset rather than its price. Attention tends to arrive with price shocks, regulatory rulings and security failures.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Readership climbed through a week in which Bitcoin surged to $80,020, up 23.7%, a rally later described as a short squeeze rather than leveraged buying. The 24 August peak sat between a shariah board clearing Bitcoin trading at Rakbank Islamic and BlackRock cutting its swap-in threshold from $25 million to $1 million.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A prediction market on which party wins the most seats in Russia's next State Duma election. United Russia is the governing party, and the contract is a price on whether the existing parliamentary order holds rather than a forecast of an open contest.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The odds climbed from 59 on Jul 30 to 74 on Aug 16 as any softer scenario receded: Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead, Ukraine launched one of its largest attacks of the war on Aug 16, and the EU foreign affairs chief moved to expand sanctions against Russia.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US–Iran ceasefire holds to a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on strikes, sanctions and diplomacy rather than on any official assessment.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: The contract sank to 68 on Aug 19 as Washington prepared "Operation Economic Outcast", the sanctions package that cut US dollar access for six Banque Misr branches and drew Iran's denunciation. It recovered to 90 by Aug 27 as Hormuz stayed navigable: Trump declared the strait clear, Iran and Oman charted a temporary corridor, and 7 tankers crossed Thursday.

wiki-nepal.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan country of about 30 million between India and China. Attention to a country page tends to be flat for months and then spike, tracking whatever brings it into the world's field of view.
wiki-nepal.recent: A glacial outburst flood tore down the Nepal–Tibet border valleys from 26 August, killing at least 160 by the first count and later passing 540 dead with 1,500 missing and 93,000 affected. No rain fell beforehand: a moraine-dammed lake failed upstream. India airlifted 37.5 tonnes of aid and sent tunnel rescuers for about 100 trapped underground.

wiki-tariff.standing: A tax a government charges on imported goods, paid at the border by the importer and usually passed into the price on the shelf. It is the oldest instrument of trade policy, and the one that invites retaliation in kind from the country on the other side.
wiki-tariff.recent: Readership tracked the US–Canada trade war. Ottawa refused US relief on heavy trucks and answered with a dollar-for-dollar list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, while Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened to cut power to the US. The 25 August peak came alongside Ford's retaliation backing; a second push followed Trump's plan to tax chips.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the US Federal Reserve targets for overnight lending between banks. It is the base price of dollar credit, and mortgages, corporate borrowing and the value of the dollar itself are priced off it.
fed-funds.recent: The target has fallen from 5.5% in Aug 2024 to 3.75%, where it has sat since Dec 2025. The direction is now in question: Fed minutes released 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and markets trimmed rate hike bets as the dollar fell against the euro. Attention has shifted to Warsh's Jackson Hole speech.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays banks on money parked with it overnight, and the floor under borrowing costs across the euro area. It sets what savers earn, what mortgages cost and how the euro trades against other currencies.
ecb-rate.recent: The rate has been cut by roughly 40% over the series, down from 3.75% in Aug 2024 to a low of 2% in Jun 2025 and 2.25% now — the ECB easing while others tighten. The Bank of Korea hiked to 3.00% in August, and Fed minutes showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force that is looking for work and cannot find it, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the number the Federal Reserve weighs against inflation when it sets interest rates.
us-unemployment.recent: The rate stands at 4.1%, down from the 4.5% peak in November 2025 and back near the 4% low of January 2025.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether JD Vance wins the 2028 US presidential election, priced as the cost of a bet paying out if he does. It tracks how traders read the Republican succession, and it moves years before a single vote is cast.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.recent: The contract drifted up from 20% on Jul 30 to 25% on Aug 29, its highest in the window. Nothing in the month's news bears on Vance himself; the prediction-market stories were about the venues rather than the race, with the Ninth Circuit ruling on Aug 28 that sports-event contracts are not swaps and a White House aide fined for betting on speeches he read early.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Marco Rubio becomes the Republican nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it tracks how a crowded, unsettled primary field is being bet on years before a vote.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.recent: The contract has drifted down from 28% on 31 July to 17% on 28 August, with nothing in the news around it about Rubio. What moved was the venue: the Ninth Circuit ruled on 28 August that a CFTC licence does not pre-empt Nevada gambling law, and Connecticut sued Kalshi the day before.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington lifts its naval blockade of Iran by a set date. It prices how traders read the pressure campaign — the odds fall when sanctions widen and rise when the strait and its shipping start moving again.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Odds halved from 24% on Aug 27 to 10% as Washington widened rather than eased the campaign: Treasury cut six Banque Misr branches out of dollar clearing on 28 Aug under "Operation Economic Outcast," and Pezeshkian conceded foreign trade has shrunk by more than a third. The IRGC meanwhile claimed a veto over Hormuz transits.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Bab el-Mandeb strait — the Red Sea gateway carrying traffic between the Suez Canal and the Indian Ocean — will be closed to shipping by a set date. Traders price the risk that war shuts one of the world's busiest sea lanes.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: The contract has fallen from 22% on Jul 30 to 5%, its lowest of the window, as traders unwound the closure bet through August. Nothing in the month's news explains the drift beyond the absence of a closure event itself.

poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Édouard Philippe, the former French prime minister and mayor of Le Havre, wins the presidency in 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field of candidates and their standing shifts.
poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.recent: The contract has barely moved over the month, holding near 26% since its Jul 30 high and touching 25 on Aug 24. Nothing in the period bears on the French race; the prediction-market news instead concerned the venues themselves, with the Ninth Circuit ruling on Aug 28 that sports-event contracts are not "swaps" and that Nevada's gambling law is not pre-empted by a CFTC licence.

poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez becomes the Democratic presidential nominee in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as the plausible field narrows or widens.
poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.recent: The contract has risen over the past month, from 13% on Jul 30 to a high of 23% on Aug 24, and has eased to 19% since. Nothing in the past month's news explains the shift.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer, a federation of some 200 million people whose government runs on crude receipts. What happens to its currency, its fuel price and its security spills into West Africa's trade and labour markets.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Readership held near its 30-day high through the Osun election results and Atiku Abubakar's pledge to restore the petrol subsidy if elected in 2027, which the APC called desperation. It has since eased to 5,689 as attention moved to Tinubu's suspension of three permanent secretaries and Abuja's pitch for Chinese upstream capital after the majors' exit.

wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.standing: The Wikipedia biography of Ukraine's president, and one of the site's most-read wartime pages. Its daily readership rises and falls with the war and with the politics around him, so the curve is a rough gauge of how closely the world is watching Kyiv.
wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.recent: The 19 August peak came as anti-corruption officers searched Zelenskyy's own office, part of a fraud investigation reported at $3.4 million that also saw another top ally fired. Readership then eased through a week of Russian missile strikes on Kyiv and an allied air-defence meeting where he sought more Patriot interceptors.

stocks:MCO.standing: The New York-listed parent of Moody's Ratings and Moody's Analytics. It sells credit ratings on sovereign and corporate debt, plus the risk data and models built around them, so its revenue rises and falls with how much new debt the world issues.
stocks:MCO.recent: The one story in view has Moody's improving its assessment of Nigeria, where foreign reserves hit a 20-year high on Friday and austerity was credited for it. That does not explain the stock, which rose about 7% over three weeks to $515 on 28 August from a $473.10 low on 6 August.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares in the world's largest consumer electronics maker, whose revenue still rests mainly on the iPhone and the services sold around it. Its supply chain and its exposure to China, Europe and app-store regulation make it a proxy for all three.
stocks:AAPL.recent: The stock fell from its late-July high to 302.3 on Aug 12 and has recovered only part of that. Apple confirmed a September 9 event for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and said in Brussels it will remove several App Store fees from October under the EU's DMA — a direct cut to services revenue.
